{"id": "8e7870fb-87b3-4507-a81f-2e2392b3725f", "role": "user", "content": [{"id": "tooluse_OvtJCTWx7wPBh6J2d0Rb3Y", "content": "[{'text': '## Documentation search results\\n\\n{\"content\":{\"result\":[{\"rank_order\":1,\"title\":\"Multiple Trails \u2013 AWS CloudTrail FAQs \u2013 AWS\",\"context\":\"### Data events\\\\n\\\\nOpen all\\\\n\\\\n#### What are data events?\\\\n\\\\nData events provide insights into the resource (data plane) operations performed on or within the resource itself. Data events are often high-volume activities and include operations such as S3 object level API operations and AWS Lambda function invoke API. Data events are deactivated by default when you configure a trail. To record CloudTrail data events, you must explicitly add the supported resources or resource types you want to collect activity on. Unlike management events, data events incur additional costs. For more information, see CloudTrail pricing .\\\\n\\\\n#### How can I consume data events?\\\\n\\\\nData events that are recorded by CloudTrail are delivered to S3, similar to management events. Once enabled, these events are also available in Amazon CloudWatch Events.\\\\n\\\\n#### What are S3 data events? How do I record them?\\\\n\\\\nS3 data events represent API activity on S3 Objects. To get CloudTrail to record these actions, you specify a S3 bucket in the data events section when creating a new trail or modifying an existing one. Any API actions on the Objects within the specified S3 bucket are recorded by CloudTrail.\\\\n\\\\n#### What are Lambda data events? How do I record them?\\\\n\\\\nLambda data events record runtime activity of your Lambda functions. With Lambda data events, you can get details on Lambda function runtime. Examples of Lambda function runtime include which IAM user or service made the Invoke API call, when the call was made, and which function was applied. All Lambda data events are delivered to an S3 bucket and CloudWatch Events. You can turn on logging for Lambda data events using the CLI or CloudTrail console and select which Lambda functions get logged by creating a new trail or editing an existing trail\",\"url\":\"https://aws.amazon.com/cloudtrail/faqs/\"},{\"rank_order\":2,\"title\":\"How can I audit deleted or missing objects from my Amazon S3 bucket?\",\"context\":\"### CloudTrail logs\\\\n\\\\nCloudTrail logs can track object-level data events in an S3 bucket, such as **GetObject**, **DeleteObject**, and **PutObject**. {"id": "207d0d0d-b7c2-4277-9ceb-b06320824e59", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "## Short answer: by default, no — and your account's trails confirm that gap

**S3 object deletes and Lambda invokes are "data events,"** which CloudTrail treats differently from the control-plane "management events" (CreateBucket, DeleteFunction, etc.) that are logged by default. Data events are **off by default** — you have to explicitly turn them on per-resource, and they cost extra. This is confirmed straight from the CloudTrail FAQ: *"Data events are deactivated by default when you configure a trail... data events are often high-volume activities and include operations such as S3 object level API operations and AWS Lambda function invoke API."*

### What I found checking your 4 trails (account `012345678901_1`)

| Trail | Management events | S3 object-level data events | Lambda Invoke data events |
|---|---|---|---|
| **IsengardTrail-DO-NOT-DELETE** (multi-region) | ✅ All | ❌ None | ❌ None |
| **nebula-single-region-trail** | ✅ All | ❌ None | ❌ None |
| **nebula-data-events-trail** | ⚠️ **None configured** | ✅ Yes — but **only for one bucket** (`nebula-audit-covered-012345678901_1`) | ❌ None |
| **JMERWIN_Org_Trail** (org trail, owned by account 012345678901_2) | Unknown — cross-account, couldn't inspect | Unknown | Unknown |

So concretely:
- **If someone deletes an object from any bucket other than `nebula-audit-covered-012345678901_1`**, it would **not** be recorded.
- **If someone invokes a Lambda function**, it would **not** be recorded anywhere — no trail has a Lambda data-event selector.
- There's also a side issue: `nebula-data-events-trail` only has the S3 data-event selector — it has no management-event selector at all, so it's not logging things like IAM, EC2, or other control-plane calls either.

**Want me to do anything with this?** I can't modify trail configurations myself (that's a write action you'd need to approve), but I can prep the exact change — e.g., broadening the S3 data event selector to all buckets, or adding a Lambda Invoke data-event selector — for your review.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
